annotation.title_clean: Ghana: Insights on Public Policies to Ensure AI's Beneficial Use as a Professional Tool (country questionnaire)
annotation.title_en: Ghana: Insights on Public Policies to Ensure AI's Beneficial Use as a Professional Tool (country questionnaire)
annotation.venue: IBA Alternative and New Law Business Structures Committee
named_instruments_referenced: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI
annotation.summary_en: Ghana chapter in an IBA questionnaire on AI in legal services. It finds no AI-specific legal framework, no AI tools in legal practice and no case law. Existing privacy, data protection, copyright and professional confidentiality rules apply, and it expects future AI regulation.
key_provisions_or_claims: No statutory definition of AI or AI regulatory framework exists in Ghana.
Constitutional privacy and Data Protection Act 2012 consent requirements constrain AI data use.
Copyright Act 2005 protects software but has no AI-specific terms.
Legal profession rules contain no AI provisions; confidentiality duties apply.
Government and ministry signal need for ethical and regulatory AI framework.
